title: Raja Yoga
author: Swami Vivekananda
description: Swami Vivekananda's Raja Yoga (1896), the landmark book that introduced classical yoga to Western readers. Based on lectures given in New York in 1895-96, the first part explains the practice and philosophy of the 'royal path' of meditation in plain modern language: the need for concentration, the first steps of posture and breathing, the doctrine of prana and the psychic prana, control of the mind, pratyahara and dharana, dhyana and samadhi, and the awakening of kundalini along the sushumna. The second part is Vivekananda's own translation of and commentary on the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, organised in the four traditional chapters on concentration, practice, powers and independence (kaivalya). Presenting yoga as an experimental science of mind grounded in Vedanta and Samkhya, the book shaped the reception of yoga, meditation and Hindu spirituality throughout the twentieth century and remains a standard introduction.
